text: When designing a REST API, following best practices ensures it is easy to use and maintain. First, keep endpoints simple and consistent, such as using `/users` for a user resource. Use appropriate HTTP status codes to communicate results clearly: `200` for success, `201` for created resources, `404` if something is not found, and `500` for server errors. Provide clear, up-to-date documentation so developers understand how to interact with your API. Lastly, implement versioning—like `/v1/users`—to avoid breaking changes for existing users when you update the API. These practices lead to a reliable, developer-friendly interface.
